root_cause.text: The fpu_vstl() inline assembly uses a compile-time constraint that indicates only 1 byte is written, but the ‘vstl’ instruction’s actual write size varies at runtime based on the ‘index’ parameter, so KMSAN falsely leaves most bytes marked as uninitialized, causing false-positive reports.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: “An inline assembly instruction 'vstl' can write varied amount of bytes depending on value of 'index' argument… clang generates kmsan write helper call depending on inline assembly constraints. Constraints are evaluated compile-time, but value of 'index' argument is known only at runtime. clang currently generates call to __msan_instrument_asm_store with 1 byte as size.” The patch adds `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size)` to manually mark the correct number of bytes as initialized.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing include of <linux/kmsan.h> to provide KMSAN instrumentation declarations needed in the header.
intent_record.what: Added `#include <linux/kmsan.h>` after `<linux/instrumented.h>` in a header guarded by `#ifndef __ASSEMBLER__`.
intent_record.how: This includes the Kernel Memory Sanitizer (KMSAN) header, making its declarations available for use in the header or its subsequent includes, preventing missing declaration errors when KMSAN is enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add KMSAN unpoison annotation after VSTL inline assembly to correctly mark destination memory as initialized.
intent_record.what: Added a call to kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size) after the inline assembly block in the fpu_vstl function.
intent_record.how: This ensures that KMSAN treats the memory region pointed by vxr as initialized after the VSTL store operation, preventing false positive uninitialized memory warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix KMSAN false positive by unpoisoning memory written by inline assembly in fpu_vstl.
intent_record.what: Added a call to kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size) after the inline assembly statement in the fpu_vstl function.
intent_record.how: The function now informs KMSAN that the memory region written by the assembly instruction is initialized, thus preventing false positive uninitialized memory warnings.
